summary: Extends the ISDN User Adaptation (IUA) protocol from RFC 3057 so that DPNSS 1 and DASS 2 signaling messages can be carried over IP, a technique called backhauling. DPNSS 1 is used to connect private branch exchanges (PBXs), and DASS 2 is a related access signaling system. It is a standards-track specification.

eli5.summary: Office phone systems have their own special language for setting up calls. This memo lets those messages ride along on the internet, like putting a letter in a bigger envelope to send it far away.

subtitle: How to carry DPNSS and DASS 2 office-phone signaling between a gateway and a controller over IP, by extending IUA.

tldr.problem: DPNSS 1 and DASS 2 signaling between PBXs and the telephone network is carried on digital lines, and call-control software on an IP network needs to receive those messages.
tldr.mechanism: The document extends the ISDN User Adaptation (IUA) protocol with a new message class, a reformatted DLCI field, DLC status messages and two extra error codes. The result is called DUA.
tldr.outcome: A Signaling Gateway can pass DPNSS/DASS 2 layer 2 events to a Media Gateway Controller over SCTP, using SCTP Payload Protocol ID 10.

today: RFC 4129 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It extends RFC 3057.

sections.title: What DUA Is For
sections.content:
RFC 4129 describes backhauling DPNSS 1 and DASS 2 messages over IP using a modified version of the ISDN User Adaptation protocol (IUA, RFC 3057). The result, the DPNSS/DASS 2 User Adaptation or DUA, is IUA plus the extensions that DPNSS/DASS 2 needs. The RFC says it aims to become an Appendix to IUA and the base for DUA implementations.

The need is to deliver Switched Circuit Network signaling from a DPNSS Signaling Gateway (SG) to a Media Gateway Controller (MGC). DPNSS is specified in ND1301:2001/03 and interconnects PBXs in a private network. DASS 2 is specified in BTNR 190 and connects PBXs to the PSTN. Unless stated otherwise, the details apply to both.
sections.eli5: Office phones have their own way of talking to set up calls. This memo teaches a box to forward that talk across the internet to the computer that runs the calls.

sections.title: DPNSS Background and Backhaul Architecture
sections.content:
DPNSS is defined between a PBX and an Access Network and extends facilities normally available only between extensions on one PBX to all extensions in a private network. It runs over a 2048 kbits/s (E1) or 1544 kbits/s (T1) digital interface. One channel carries signaling: channel 16 on E1 and channel 24 on T1. These D-channels, plus the associated DPNSS channels, form a DPNSS Link.

A Data Link Connection (DLC) is the level 2 process that controls transfer of level 3 messages for one DPNSS channel. DPNSS supports 60 DLCs (30 real and 30 virtual), while DASS 2 supports 30 (all real). A real channel has an associated traffic channel; a virtual channel does not.

In the proposed architecture the PBX talks DPNSS to the SG. The SG terminates DPNSS layer 2 and uses DUA, SCTP and IP towards the MGC, which runs DPNSS layer 3. A Nodal Interworking Function (NIF) joins the two sides in the SG.
sections.eli5: The phone system sends its messages to a middle box. The middle box puts them in an internet envelope and sends them to the computer that decides how to connect the calls.

sections.title: Changes to the IUA Message Header
sections.content:
DUA introduces a new message class, 13, for DPNSS/DASS2 Boundary Primitives Transport Messages (DPTM), so they are not confused with IUA or its other extensions such as V5 or GR-303. Management (0), ASP State Maintenance (3) and ASP Traffic Maintenance (4) remain valid.

The IUA message header MUST be used, but the DLCI field is formatted per ND1301:2001/03: 7 reserved bits, a V-bit, a zero bit, a 6-bit channel number and a final one bit. With the V-bit set to 1 the action applies to the single DLC named by the channel number. With 0 it applies to all DLCs and the channel number is ignored. Only Establish and Release messages use the V-bit.

Valid channel numbers are 0 to 63 for DPNSS and 0 to 31 for DASS 2. Unit Data messages are invalid, since DPNSS layer 2 has no unit data primitive; the Data Request and Indication messages (types 1 and 2) are used instead.
sections.eli5: Each message has an address label saying which phone line it is about. A special flag on the label says whether the message is for one line or for all the lines at once.

sections.title: DLC Status Messages
sections.content:
DUA adds three Management-class message types to report DLC state: 5 DLC Status Request, 6 DLC Status Confirm and 7 DLC Status Indication. The Confirm and Indication carry a new DLC Status parameter, tag 0x12, which uses two bits per DLC.

  • 00 Out Of Service
  • 01 Reset Attempted
  • 10 Reset Completed
  • 11 Information Transfer

For an E1 interface the parameter has slots for D0 to D63, with D0 and D16 not applicable because timeslot 0 is used for framing and timeslot 16 for signaling. For a T1 interface D23 is not applicable because that timeslot is used for signaling. For DASS 2 the value 00 is invalid because its DLCs have no such state, and the Idle state is transient and local, so it has no value.
sections.eli5: The status message is a report card with two tiny boxes per phone line. The boxes say whether each line is off, trying to start, ready, or busy carrying messages.

sections.title: Management Messages and Error Codes
sections.content:
Only the Notify and Error management messages are valid in DUA; the TEI Status messages are not used. The Error message is sent when an invalid value or unrecognized message arrives. DUA keeps the IUA error codes, except that 0x0a, 0x0b and 0x0c are invalid because they are specific to ISDN.

Two new codes are added: 0x1c Channel Number out of range, sent for a channel number above 63 for DPNSS or 31 for DASS 2, and 0x1d Channel Number not configured.
sections.eli5: If a message names a phone line that does not exist or was never set up, the receiver sends back a note saying which of those two mistakes it was.

sections.title: Message Sequences and SCTP Payload ID
sections.content:
The RFC shows flows between the PBX, the SG and the MGC, assuming an active association between MGC and SG. To reset one DLC, the MGC sends an Establish Request with indicator 1. The SG sends SABMR to the PBX and returns an Establish Confirm after the PBX answers UA. If retransmissions over NT1 and NT2 expire, the SG sends a Release Indication (RELEASE_OTHER) instead.

To reset all DLCs, the MGC sends an Establish Request with indicator 0. The SG resets each DLC, confirms, and the MGC then issues a Status Request to learn each DLC's state. Data moves with Data Request and Data Indication. Release works like Establish: indicator 1 for one DLC, 0 for all.

The SCTP Payload Protocol ID for DUA is 10, assigned by IANA. The IUA value MAY also be used, for example to backhaul ISDN and DPNSS over the same association, but separate IDs (10 for DUA and 1 for IUA) are recommended even then.
sections.eli5: The controller asks the middle box to wake up a phone line. The middle box knocks on the phone system's door and reports back whether anyone answered.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 4129 adds no security text of its own. It says that the security considerations of IUA (Section 6 of RFC 3057) and of the SIGTRAN security document, RFC 3788, apply to it as well.
sections.eli5: It uses the same safety rules as the protocol it extends, instead of making new ones.
